content.text: I'll start by reading the file and the finding's target line.

input.command: cat -n src/git-auth.ts; echo ---CONFIG---; cat -n src/config.ts; echo ---LS---; find . -path ./node_modules -prune -o -type f \( -name "*.ts" -o -name "*.js" -o -name "*.json" -o -name "*.md" \) -print | grep -v node_modules
input.description: Read git-auth.ts and config.ts, list repo files

input.command: grep -rn "remoteUrl\|cloneRepo\|gitAuthArgs\|github.com" src/ package.json; echo ---ROUTES---; cat -n src/routes.ts; echo ---API---; cat -n src/api.ts; echo ---STORE---; cat -n src/store.ts; echo ---TASKS---; cat -n src/tasks.ts; echo ---PKG---; cat -n package.json
input.description: Find remoteUrl origins and callers; read routes, api, store, tasks, package.json

input.reason: src/worktree.ts:15 calls gitAuthArgs(repo.remoteUrl, SERVICE_TOKEN) and then `git clone repo.remoteUrl` with no validation of the URL. The only caller, registerRepo in src/routes.ts:19-22, takes remoteUrl from req.body, checks only that it is truthy, and passes it to cloneRepo. SERVICE_TOKEN is process.env.HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN (src/config.ts:4). gitAuthArgs (src/git-auth.ts:7-12) attaches `-c http.extraHeader=Authorization: Bearer <token>` whenever remoteUrl.includes("github.com") — a substring check rather than a host check — so a user-chosen URL such as https://evil.example/github.com/x or https://github.com.evil.example/x receives the service token. The finding's central claim holds; its "whatever host the URL names" clause is narrowed to reflect the substring guard. No test files exist in the tree (package.json only defines `node --test`).
input.summary: cloneRepo sends service token to any user-supplied URL containing github.com

findings.text: `cloneRepo` passes the user-supplied `remoteUrl` straight to `gitAuthArgs` with the service token, so `git clone` sends the token to whatever host the URL names once the URL contains the substring `github.com` anywhere.
findings.reason: The first claim holds: src/worktree.ts:15 passes repo.remoteUrl and SERVICE_TOKEN to gitAuthArgs with no validation, and the sole caller registerRepo (src/routes.ts:19-22) takes remoteUrl from req.body with only a truthiness check. The second claim reaches too far: gitAuthArgs (src/git-auth.ts:8-11) returns no header unless remoteUrl.includes("github.com"), so a URL such as https://evil.example/repo does not receive the token. Because the guard is a substring check rather than a host check, URLs like https://evil.example/github.com/x or https://github.com.evil.example/x still pass it and git sends the unscoped http.extraHeader to that host, so the central claim stands. Narrowed the condition to match the code.

input.severity_reason: Exploitable credential exfiltration: any authenticated user can call registerRepo (src/routes.ts:18, no admin check) with a remoteUrl such as https://attacker.example/github.com/x; gitAuthArgs's substring check (src/git-auth.ts:8) passes it and git clone sends `Authorization: Bearer <HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN>` to the attacker's server, disclosing the service's GitHub token.
